items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: And my wife went to the Lieutenant, to speak to him on my behalf. His name was Lieutenant Danzinger.

ctx.x: That’s right. We were all sent overseas just the day before I was transferred. In other words, after I was transferred to the Army Air Force Band at Ft. Dix, they went right

overseas. We were at the Port of Embarkation, Monk, at Camp Kilmer, New Jersey. I’ll never forget that. And we knew we were going to go overseas in a matter of a day or two. And my wife went to the Lieutenant, to speak to him on my behalf. His name was Lieutenant Danzinger. Look how I remember that name, 50 years ago. D-A-N-Z-I-N-G- E-R. Lieutenant Danzinger. But before he was able to give me the transfer, Monk, my wife had to go to see the major of that battalion. And his name was Major Fox. She spoke to him. My…

Well the music that you were attracted to and you began to play, did you and the rest of the players think of it as — I’m trying to figure out how to say this — was it the popular music of the day or did you think of it as you were playing something from the past?
